page: Microsoft Azure E20_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual instance built on the Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization platform. It is powered by a dedicated 64-bit Intel Xeon 8272CL processor operating at a base frequency of 2.6 GHz. The configuration allocates 20 virtual CPUs across 10 physical cores via hyperthreading, backed by 32 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 35 MB L3 cache. Instruction set capabilities include AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, AES, BMI2, and ADX, enabling vector mathematical computations and cryptographic routines.

The instance is equipped with 160 GB of RAM, establishing an allocation ratio of 8 GB of memory per vCPU. It does not bundle local disk storage, nor does it supply a GPU accelerator or complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Storage configurations consequently depend entirely on external volume attachments, which should be considered when planning disk-intensive workflows.

Synthetic testing reflects middle-tier performance profiles across core processing and system throughput. The system records a multi-core score of 18,613.51 in stress-ng and 8,313 in Geekbench multi-core evaluation, with a PassMark CPU rating of 19,123.19. Memory tests indicate uncached large-block read speeds of 88.48 GB/sec and write speeds of 43.27 GB/sec, while cached small-block reads achieve 1,034.46 GB/sec. Application testing demonstrates 16.52 million Redis SET operations per second and 13.48 GB/sec in static web throughput. Single-threaded compression shows lower relative efficiency, with gzip registering 23.81 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression achieving 8.63 GB/sec. Similarly, 7B model LLM prompt processing yields 29.26 tokens per second.

Given its high memory-to-core ratio and solid multi-core computational throughput, the E20_v4 represents a balanced choice for applications demanding extensive memory pools without requiring dedicated GPU acceleration. Typical production deployments include in-memory databases such as Redis, enterprise relational databases, distributed caching layers, and large memory-bound extract, transform, load pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure E20_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. Powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8272CL processor clocked at 2.6 GHz, the instance delivers 20 dedicated vCPUs derived from 10 physical cores with multithreading enabled, supported by a 35 MB L3 cache and AVX-512 instruction extensions. With 160 GB of system memory, it maintains an 8 GB memory-to-vCPU ratio suited for in-memory operations. The instance does not include integrated local disk storage or hardware GPU acceleration, requiring reliance on external storage architectures. Benchmark data places the system in the middle tier for CPU computation, achieving 18,613.51 in stress-ng multi-core testing, 8,313 in Geekbench multi-core, and 16.52 million Redis SET operations per second, though single-threaded compression performance measures in the lower quartile. The instance offers resource density tailored for in-memory caching, mid-sized relational databases, enterprise data analytics, and memory-bound background processing pipelines.
